Thawing of frozen tis- sue following surgery may be painful and prolonged spraying onto the skin can cause chemical frostbite. Freezing may also distort the histological structure of biopsy specimens. Ethyl chlo- ride should not be applied to broken skin or mucous membranes. Uses and Administration Owing to its low boiling-point and the intense cold produced by evaporation, ethyl chloride has been used as a local anaesthetic in minor surgery but such use is not generally recommended. It has also been used topically for the relief of pain and to test the effectiveness of regional anaesthesia. Ethyl chloride was former- ly used as an inhalational anaesthetic but has no place in modern anaesthetic practice.
